LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Tiro.title: legion recruit
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Tiro.description: [PAWN_nameDef] signed on with the legion at eighteen and marched until [PAWN_possessive] feet bled. The drill sergeants taught [PAWN_objective] to dig a ditch, raise a palisade and hold a line before they ever taught [PAWN_objective] to fight.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Faber.title: legion smith
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Faber.description: For years [PAWN_nameDef] kept the forges of a frontier fort burning, hammering out gladii, mending mail and shoeing the officers' horses. [PAWN_pronoun] can tell good iron from bad by the sound it makes.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Architectus.title: aqueduct architect
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Architectus.description: [PAWN_nameDef] designed arches that carried water across valleys. [PAWN_pronoun] checks every wall with a plumb line and cannot pass a crooked one without frowning.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Senator.title: junior senator
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Senator.description: [PAWN_nameDef] spoke in the senate of Nova Roma, argued over grain laws and learned that every friendship has a price. [PAWN_pronoun] considers digging and hauling beneath a citizen of [PAWN_possessive] rank.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Medicus.title: field medicus
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Medicus.description: [PAWN_nameDef] followed the legion from battle to battle with a bag of bronze tools and vinegar-soaked bandages. [PAWN_pronoun] has stitched more wounds than [PAWN_pronoun] can count.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Agricola.title: villa farmer
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Agricola.description: [PAWN_nameDef] worked the terraced olive groves and wheat fields of a country villa. [PAWN_pronoun] knows the calendar of sowing by heart and distrusts anyone who has never held a plough.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Centurio.title: veteran centurion
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Centurio.description: [PAWN_nameDef] commanded eighty legionaries for a decade and carries the vine staff of [PAWN_possessive] rank. [PAWN_pronoun] is hard, fair and loud, and [PAWN_possessive] soldiers would follow [PAWN_objective] into a river.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Mercator.title: road merchant
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Mercator.description: [PAWN_nameDef] drove mule trains along the stone roads, selling wine, oil and gossip from town to town. [PAWN_pronoun] can price a cart of goods at a glance.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_CastraChild.title: camp child
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_CastraChild.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up among the tents and earthworks of a marching camp, running errands for soldiers and learning the bugle calls before [PAWN_possessive] letters.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Scriba.title: scribe's pupil
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Scriba.description: [PAWN_nameDef] spent [PAWN_possessive] childhood copying laws onto wax tablets in the tabularium, where a single blot meant a beating.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Subura.title: street urchin
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Subura.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in the crowded tenements of the lower city, where [PAWN_pronoun] learned to steal bread, climb roofs and talk [PAWN_possessive] way out of trouble.
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Villa.title: villa child
LanguageData.HE_Roma_BS_Villa.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up on a country estate among vines, goats and storytelling grandparents.
